# Tutorial : Portfolio with Quarto and Jupyter

In this tutorial we will create a portfolio website using Quarto and Jupyter notebooks.

[go.uwe.ac.uk/portfolio2](https://go.uwe.ac.uk/portfolio2)

## Prerequisites

1. VSCode with Quarto, Jupyter plugins installed
2. [Quarto CLI installed](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) on your computer (or point to RStudio Quarto binary if you have that installed)

## More Docs and Help

[Quarto Blog Documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-blog.html)

## Create a new Quarto Project
1. Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) -> Quarto: Create New Project
2. Select "New Quarto Blog"
3. Name your project "Portfolio"
4. Select location on your computer
5. Open the folder in VSCode

## Change the Theme
[Available Themes](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html)

In _qaurto.yml change the theme to eg "vapor"

```yaml
format:
    html:
        theme: vapor
```

## Add an Example Notebook
1.Create a new post as a subfolder and get a demo notebook
(nb [Wget for Windows](https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/wget.htm) if you don't have it)

```bash
cd posts
mkdir clustering
wget https://akmand.github.io/_sources/ml/SK6_Clustering.ipynb
```

2. Add front matter to the top of the notebook
```yaml
---

title: "K-Means Demo"
author: "Paul Matthews (copied from D.Akman)"
date: "2026-02-01"
categories: [news, code, analysis]
toc: true
toc-depth: 2

---
```

## Publishing to GitHub Pages

[See Quarto Docs here](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html), we with use the GitHub Actions method.

1. Create a new repository on GitHub called "portfolio"
2. In VSCode initialize a git repository in your local folder
```bash
git init
git remote add origin git@github.com:{your user}/{repo name}.git
```
3. Create .gitignore file and add 

```.gitignore
_site
.quarto

```

4. Commit changes
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"

```
5.publish to GitHub

```bash
quarto publish gh-pages
```
